name: Split-Strike Long Combo (OTM Risk Reversal)
summary: Sell an OTM put and buy an OTM call in the same expiry, usually structured for zero net cost; bullish exposure with a flat dead zone between the strikes.

legs.strike_rule: OTM call whose premium approximately equals the put credit -- typically 0.20-0.30 delta. Tune the call strike until the net is within +/-$0.05 of zero for a 'zero-cost' structure.

max_loss: UNDEFINED below the put strike -- (put strike * 100) - net credit
breakevens: if opened flat: below = put strike; above = call strike. Adjust by the net debit/credit per share.

greeks.delta: positive, roughly +0.40 to +0.60 per unit at entry
greeks.gamma: positive above the call strike, negative below the put strike
greeks.theta: near zero at entry; becomes positive if price sits between the strikes
greeks.vega: near zero at entry; long vega above, short vega below

when_to_use: The classic 'get long using the skew': equity put skew means the OTM put you sell is richer in IV than the OTM call you buy, so a zero-cost structure gets you a call further out than symmetry would suggest. Used by institutions to establish leveraged bullish exposure cheaply.
entry_rules: BLOCKED ON THIS ACCOUNT. The short put is uncovered -- Level 4, unavailable on Alpaca, and rejected by the MLeg covered-legs rule.

Defined-risk substitute: sell a bull PUT SPREAD (defined) and use the credit to buy a call or a call spread -- that structure IS Level 3 legal as two separate MLeg orders and captures the same skew idea with a floor.
If it were enabled: put skew condition 25-delta put IV - 25-delta call IV >= 4 vol points; net cost between -$0.05 and +$0.05; both legs 0.20-0.30 delta; DTE 45-90.
Sizing would have to assume the short put is assigned: (put strike * 100 * contracts) <= 25% of equity.
management_rules: If enabled: take profit when the long call reaches 2x its theoretical entry premium, or when the underlying exceeds the call strike by 1.5 ATR.
Close the whole structure at 21 DTE.
Stop: close if the underlying trades below the short put strike.
If the short put goes ITM, close it and keep the call only if you still want the exposure -- never roll a tested short put down and out on an account that cannot take delivery.
exit_rules: Flat by 15:45 ET on expiration day.
ASSIGNMENT GUARD: close the short put whenever it is ITM with extrinsic < $0.10, and unconditionally if the underlying is below (put strike + $0.05) at 15:30 ET on expiry day.
Close or roll by 21 DTE as a standing rule.
assignment_risk: The short put is uncovered. Assignment delivers 100 shares per contract at the put strike, unfunded. The long call is at a higher strike and provides no protection below.
buying_power: Reg-T naked put margin on the short leg, less the premium of the long call. Not available on Alpaca.
liquidity_needs: OTM strikes on both sides; OI >= 500, bid/ask <= 10% of mid.
common_mistakes: Reading 'zero cost' as 'zero risk'; not sizing for assignment on the put; picking the call strike by dollars instead of by matching premium.
zero_dte_notes: No time for the structure to work and immediate assignment exposure. Not permitted.
family: Two-leg verticals and same-expiry two-leg combos (call/put verticals, straddles, strangles, guts, synthetics/risk reversals, ratio verticals and backspreads)
blocked_because: needs Alpaca options level 4; this account is level 3. Alpaca rejects it with 'account not eligible to trade uncovered option contracts'. Raising the level is an Alpaca approval, not a code change.
